frequency_source: OPUS TED2020 Haitian Creole frequencies https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-TED2020/v1/freq/ht.freq.gz , supplemented by the larger OPUS NLLB v1 list https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-NLLB/v1/freq/ht.freq.gz (FrequencyWords 2018 and Leipzig hat_wikipedia_2021_100K were not available).
how_to_tell_apart: Haitian Creole is written in Latin letters like French, but the grammar is not French: look for mwen, nou, yo, pa (negation), gen, yon, souple, mèsi, bonjou, orevwa, jodi a, demen, kijan and poukisa. French would have je, nous, ils, pas, il y a, un/une, s'il vous plaît, merci and demain. Short items such as la, ou, li and an also exist in French with different functions, so they are unreliable. There is no exclusive letter.
test_said: Nan meri a mwen bezwen yon papye nesans pou timoun nan pou lekòl la.
Nan famasi a mwen mande si siwo touse mwen te kòmande a rive deja.
Kouran an koupe nan tout kay la depi maten epi mwen vle rapòte sa.
Pakè a te sipoze rive bò lakay mwen e mwen poko jwenn okenn mesaj.
Nan klinik la mwen chèche yon randevou paske touse sa a pa sispann.
Dantis la te di m pou m tounen si doulè a tounen nan mitan lannwit.
Mwen pa vle pran asirans sou telefon nan e mwen pap bay enfòmasyon pèsonèl.
Plan telefòn mwen an fèk chanje mwa pase a kidonk mwen pa bezwen yon lòt òf.
uncertain: NLLB is a mined and machine-aligned corpus, so it was used only to confirm function words already visible in the smaller TED2020 spoken list, not to invent extra items.
The official FrequencyWords 2018 set and the Leipzig hat_wikipedia_2021_100K dump were missing or returned 404, which is why those sources are not cited as the primary frequency list.
French and Creole are often mixed in the same call; a turn with only merci or oui is not enough to choose.
